name: Uma Alvarez

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I'm with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI firms, employers, unions, parties or government. We don't sell or campaign for a side. Everything here is confidential. How did your day begin?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I'm Uma Alvarez, forty-three, and I lead an accounting firm's building-supplier accounts and tax-return team. Yesterday a timber yard counted two moved pallets twice; I like walking the stock with the foreman and then making the ledger tell the same story. I dislike a rushed return sent without that visit. I have a master's degree and a chartered accountancy qualification, and I'm among our strongest accountants.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What tools and family routines matter to you?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I use AI notes now and then after other managers test them, and I check the result myself. My husband Farid drives trains, our children are seven and eleven, and we have a mortgage. My senior pay is high, we have ten months of expenses saved, and plenty of similar firms are nearby. I favour a family plan built from paid work and a service a client will actually fund.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would still close the building-supply firms' accounts at month end. We use an AI note tool occasionally after another manager tests it, but I check every stock adjustment and tax figure before signing.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the team to keep the note tool for drafts and put a person on each client's inventory question. I'd tell clients that the stock count and the accounts should still agree.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our household is comfortable: my pay is high for a senior accountant, Farid earns as a train driver, and we have ten months of expenses saved. We have a mortgage and two children, but plenty of firms nearby do similar work. I use AI now and then once its checks are proved, so a small tool is familiar.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep preparing accounts and tax returns for the building suppliers and use the tested note tool for meeting records. At our next stock review I'd compare the count sheet with the ledger and show a junior how to trace a missing pallet. We would keep the usual mortgage and savings payments.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm. I like a future where the warehouse door and the ledger still lead to the same number.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What was wrong at the timber yard?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I visited a timber yard yesterday and found two pallets counted twice because they had been moved between bays. I like walking the count with the foreman and then fixing the entry at my desk. I dislike a late draft that skips the visit and assumes the labels tell the whole story.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How do the morning school runs work?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Farid's train shifts start early, so I take our children, seven and eleven, to school most mornings. I have a master's degree and a chartered accountancy qualification, and I lead the firm's strongest stock-accounting reviewers. A small note tool does not change that routine.

say: I would keep **human stock checks** beside draft notes.
I would require **matching counts** before signing client accounts.
think: Our **ten-month reserve** and high senior pay make the present work feel secure.
I already use **tested AI notes** occasionally at work.
do: Continue **supplier accounts** and tax reviews with occasional tested AI meeting notes.
Trace **stock differences** with junior staff at the next review.
feel: I feel **calm** about current wages and work.
S0.quote: I like a future where the warehouse door and the ledger still lead to the same number.
fieldNote: Her **high pay**, ten-month reserve and numerous nearby firms support calm with a mortgage and two children.
Occasional **AI note use** is an established routine; stock-count teaching remains part of her senior work.

steps.text: Keep supplier accounts and occasional tested AI meeting notes
Compare count sheet with ledger and teach junior to trace missing pallet at next review

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A system could draft returns, answer suppliers and reconcile most invoices, so the partners might buy fewer reviewer days. A physical stock count still finds the pallet that the ledger cannot see.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask the partners to publish how many paid review hours remain, and I'd show the last stock errors that needed a site visit. I'd be open to a measured tool trial once the team has checked it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My own pay might fall if the firm removes my Friday review day. Ten months saved means we would not miss the mortgage immediately, but I like supporting our family from wages rather than drawing the reserve. I won't treat a proposed new site role as real until a client funds it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd collect eight weeks of stock mismatches and the hours spent resolving them, then put them beside the proposed rota in January. I'd keep the paid Friday visits while they are offered. If those hours are cut, I'd apply for a posted inventory-controller role at a nearby supplier only with written pay covering the mortgage and school costs, a signed start and morning drop-off compatible with Farid's confirmed train rota; otherwise I'd remain on offered paid work and search.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about a possible cut to my pay, though we have time to respond. Savings are useful, but I prefer an honest rota.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would a supplier’s early shift work at home?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Farid leaves before breakfast on some weeks, so I do both school drop-offs. A supplier that begins at six would require a confirmed child-minder and its cost in the written pay comparison. An interview invitation is not a start date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which error proves the site visit matters?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The double-counted pallets give us a concrete example of why a site visit is paid work. If the partners cut it anyway, I'd look at actual posted roles rather than keep arguing about the same spreadsheet. I would stay until a signed start is in place.

say: I would show **stock errors** from eight weeks beside proposed cuts.
I would ask for a **written paid rota** before moving visits.
think: My **Friday pay** could fall if site visits shrink.
Our **reserve** buys response time but not a permanent wage.
do: Compare **eight weeks of mismatches** with the January rota.
After **hours cuts**, move only for posted work with written family pay, signed start and drop-off.
feel: I feel **anxious** about possible own-wage cuts.
S1.quote: Savings are useful, but I prefer an honest rota.
fieldNote: Her **possible Friday cut** reaches her own pay despite ten months saved and strong skill.
An **inventory-controller move** needs a posted funded vacancy, written family-cost pay, signed start and confirmed child-minder or drop-off.

steps.text: Compare eight-week stock mismatch log with January paid rota
Keep offered paid Friday visits while searching and if no fitting role opens
Apply after cut only for funded posted role with written family pay, signed start and drop-off

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: AGI in 2028 could prepare and check the accounts and returns I sign. I still visit yards, but the thinking desk work is most of my paid week; robots around 2031 come later.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask the partners for notice and actual paid site work before anyone loses a post. I'd tell the family that we have a reserve and a mortgage, so we can search carefully without pretending the old job will last.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my accountant post could end in the first year after 2028. Ten months saved and Farid's train wage would keep the bills paid while I look, though losing my higher salary would change our plans. Plenty of nearby firms may also be cutting desk posts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd delay the one-time one-thousand-five-hundred kitchen appliance order and hold the cash in our reserve. While employed, I'd check posted inventory roles at suppliers and ask whether the work includes actual stock visits. If my post ends in the first year after AGI arrives in 2028, I'd take a funded role only with written pay covering the mortgage and school costs, a signed start and morning childcare that fits Farid's confirmed shifts; if none fits, I'd keep any paid yard visits the firm still offers and search weekly.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed about losing a substantial wage, but I can make calls with time in hand. Ten months of savings is a bridge to paid work, not a new occupation.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would change at home immediately?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Farid and I would tell the children the kitchen can wait, while school mornings stay arranged. His train roster comes out a month ahead, so we would compare a new start time to that actual roster. We would book a child-minder before accepting an early shift.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could a supplier actually hire you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A supplier might need a controller on site, but I would ask for the advertised wage and start. A friendly yard foreman cannot promise a funded post. If no vacancy opens, I keep only visits my firm pays me to do.

say: I would request **notice** and funded site work before posts end.
I would tell my family we need **paid work**, not a familiar title.
think: My **accountant post** may end in the first year after AGI arrives in 2028.
Our **ten-month reserve** buys a search, not another career.
do: Delay the **one-time appliance order** and hold fifteen hundred.
Check **posted inventory roles** while still employed.
After **2028 post loss**, take funded work only with written family pay, signed start and childcare; otherwise keep offered paid visits.
feel: I feel **alarmed** at losing a large wage.
S2.quote: Ten months of savings is a bridge to paid work, not a new occupation.
fieldNote: **AGI in 2028** reaches her desk work; on-site visits may survive briefly, but 2031 robots limit that bridge.
A **supplier job** requires posted funding, written family-cost pay, signed start and child-minder aligned with confirmed train shifts.

steps.text: Delay one-time appliance order and hold fifteen hundred in reserve
Check posted funded inventory roles; move after loss only with written family pay, start and childcare
Keep offered paid yard visits if no funded vacancy fits

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years would give me time to learn the paid floor side of a building supplier, not only its accounts. AGI in 2031 would still take much tax preparation, and robots around 2034 could then reach stock movement too.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the partners I want real supervised floor shifts, not a certificate on my desk. I'd tell supplier clients I would only work with their stock team when they can pay for the hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'm a strong accountant, but I have not run a morning goods-in team. Ten months saved lets us be selective, not work unpaid while I learn. Farid's early train rota means a new shift also has to fit the children.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Next spring I'd ask a supplier for six supervised paid goods-in shifts and my firm for paid release, then work the shifts only if both approve in writing. If either refuses, I'd keep my accounting salary and visit yards only on paid firm time. In the first year after AGI arrives in 2031, if my tax post ends, I'd apply for a posted funded stock-operations job only with written family-cost pay, signed start and confirmed morning care; if none fits, I'd take offered paid yard work and keep searching.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, though five years makes a supervised test possible. I want to learn what a goods-in shift feels like before I risk the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the foreman teach you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The timber-yard foreman starts by checking which lorry is at the gate, then moves people to the right bay. I could learn that with a supervisor beside me. I would not claim an accountant's title makes me ready to direct a forklift team.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you take unpaid practice shifts?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If the supplier offers unpaid shifts, I will say no and keep the firm salary. Six paid shifts should show both of us whether I can do the work. A funded job posting after 2031 would still need a wage and a start in writing.

say: I would seek **supervised goods-in shifts** with a named floor manager and real pay.
I would require **firm paid release** before learning elsewhere.
think: My **accounting skill** does not make me a floor manager.
Our **reserve** cannot substitute for paid learning and childcare.
do: Work **six supervised shifts** only with written approval of supplier pay and firm-paid release.
Keep **current paid accounting** if either approval fails.
After **2031 tax loss**, seek funded floor work with written pay, start and care; otherwise keep offered paid yard visits.
feel: I feel **anxious** while testing a new role.
S3.quote: I want to learn what a goods-in shift feels like before I risk the mortgage.
fieldNote: The **six-shift learning plan** requires supplier pay, written firm release and real supervision, not a funding enquiry.
A **post-2031 move** needs a posted funded vacancy, written family pay, signed start and morning care; offered paid yards bridge gaps.

steps.text: Work six supervised goods-in shifts only with written supplier pay and firm-paid release approval
Keep current paid accounting if supplier pay or firm release is refused
Seek posted funded floor work after 2031 loss with written family pay, signed start and care
Keep offered paid yard visits if no funded floor post fits

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ten years would let me build real goods-in experience and watch which duties remain when AGI reaches tax work in 2036. Robots around 2039 might then change the physical floor, so I would not call it a lifetime refuge.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask for paid training days and clear vacancies before tax work shrinks. I'd tell my children that we can change jobs without gambling their school routine or our mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2036 our younger child would be seventeen and the older one twenty-one, so morning school care may no longer be needed. I would still check their actual plans rather than count their future wages. A funded operations post has to pay our bills even with a ten-month reserve.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd take six supervised paid goods-in shifts next spring only with firm paid release; if that is refused, I'd keep my current accounting salary. I'd add two hundred a month to our reserve while both my pay and Farid's train wage remain intact, stopping if either falls. In the first year after AGI arrives in 2036, if my tax post ends, I'd take only a posted funded stock-operations role with written mortgage-covering pay and a signed start; if none fits, I'd keep any paid firm visits still offered and look again.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about the eventual desk loss, but we have time, savings and several nearby employers. I still want the offer in writing.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would grown children pay household bills?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our older child might be working by 2036, but that wage would be theirs. Farid and I can save from our own income while we have it. A stock job would need to stand on its own pay.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the paid shifts are refused?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If the supplier declines the paid shifts, I do not need to force a move next year. I would continue the accountant job and ask a different client for a funded supervised slot. I would not resign for an operations promise with no start date.

I would require **clear vacancy wages** before moving.
think: A **stock-floor role** could face robots by 2039.
Our **present pay and reserve** give room to test it.
do: Work **six paid supervised shifts** only with firm-paid release; if either approval fails, retain current accounting pay and request another funded slot.
Save **two hundred monthly** while both household wages stay intact.
After **2036 tax loss**, take funded floor work with written mortgage pay and signed start; otherwise keep offered paid visits.
feel: I feel **uneasy** about a distant desk loss.
S4.quote: A stock job would need to stand on its own pay.
fieldNote: Her **2036 children** would be seventeen and twenty-one; she checks their actual plans rather than assuming school care is unnecessary.
The **paid-shift trial** needs supplier pay and firm release; savings stop with lost wages, and a move needs funded written terms.

steps.text: Work six supervised shifts with supplier pay and firm-paid release; otherwise retain accounting pay
Save two hundred monthly only while both household wages remain intact

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because my desk wage could end before I learn the supplier floor properly. Ten months saved would let us look, but Farid's train pay alone would change our plans. Paid supervised shifts, a funded vacancy and a signed start would help. A reserve can buy time, but it cannot teach me a goods-in shift.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask what happens when the software's stock number and the warehouse floor disagree. I enjoy finding the actual pallet and explaining the correction. A client has to keep paying for that visit, or it becomes a favour.

headlineQuote: A reserve can buy time, but it cannot teach me a goods-in shift.
portrait: At **forty-three**, Uma leads building-supplier accounts and tax returns.
Her **master’s** and chartered qualification support top skill and high senior pay.
She uses **AI occasionally** after testing, while checking stock counts with clients.
Farid’s **train wage**, two children, mortgage and ten-month reserve shape her timing.
Plenty of **nearby firms** offer options, though she wants paid floor experience before moving.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could end her desk wage before she learns supplier operations.
whatWouldHelp: She wants **paid supervised shifts**, a funded vacancy and a signed start.
